markdown_report:
At 20% progress, prioritize a small, calibrated execution audit before extending temporal diagnostics or changing GRU4Rec.

Three starting-point insights guide this choice. First, all four categories fail final-feature checks, with maximum errors of 0.000163–0.000633. This blocks temporal interpretation but does not identify the defect. Second, zero reported valid-feature and candidate-score errors coexist with those failures. Comparisons need explicit identities and coverage before their agreement is informative. Third, strong sampled training margins establish fitted separation. They cannot substantiate current-intent alignment or validation improvement.

Three literature insights sharpen the approach. PyTorch documents that batched and singleton computations can differ numerically, so separate repeated execution from indexing checks. CheckList distinguishes functionality, invariance, and directional tests, motivating explicit expected outcomes. DeepMutation motivates temporary injected faults to test whether a diagnostic detects the failures it claims to detect; its original evidence concerns image classification, so recommendation applicability remains a hypothesis.

These insights organize three directions: establish execution identity, calibrate diagnostic sensitivity, then measure temporal dependence. The framework is:

| Layer | Controlled comparison | Evidence supplied |
|---|---|---|
| Readout | Same feature tensor, independently gathered final position | Indexing consistency |
| Execution | Fixed history across batching/padding configurations | Numerical or semantic discrepancy |
| Calibration | Unchanged control versus temporary fault | Probe detection coverage |
| Behavior | Intact versus fixed-candidate shuffles | Conditional ranking sensitivity |

Three atomic ideas follow. Scores are originality/potential/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

- **Calibrated readout audit — 4/8/3.** Originality: useful integration, established components. Potential: resolves a concrete blocker, fixed fixtures have limited coverage. Difficulty: bounded inference, careful adapter handling required. References: PyTorch, CheckList, DeepMutation.
- **Lag-specific hidden-state restoration — 6/7/7.** Originality: transfers activation patching to GRU recommendation, transfer remains incremental. Potential: localizes computational contributions, corrupted histories complicate interpretation. Difficulty: no extra predictor, faithful recurrent replay is demanding. References: Zhang–Nanda, Theory of Gating.
- **Evidence-grounded specification contrast sets — 4/6/5.** Originality: useful recommendation adaptation, established annotation design. Potential: exposes unsupported relevance claims, available text cannot establish user requirements. Difficulty: no retraining, reliable annotation is costly. References: CheckList, FEVER.

Select the **calibrated readout audit**. Independently gather the last nonpadding position from one cached feature tensor and compare it with the actual readout before comparing separate forwards. Record nonempty comparison counts and elementwise tolerance violations. Then test temporary wrong-index, row-swap, and candidate-permutation faults alongside unchanged controls; mark inapplicable mutations explicitly. Preserve checkpoint bytes and restore all state.

Only after relevant checks pass should the fixed-length full-shuffle/final-item-fixed panel resume. Its contrast compares intervention distributions; it does not isolate final-item importance. Preserve one GRU4Rec checkpoint per category and use only official macro validation HR@10 for selection.

idea.description: Implement a mutation-calibrated, same-tensor readout audit for the supplied GRU4Rec, separating indexing consistency from differences between independent forward executions before resuming temporal-sensitivity measurements.
idea.motivation: All four supplied category diagnostics fail final-feature consistency while reporting zero aligned-feature and candidate-score errors. Those measurements do not identify whether the cause is indexing, separate-forward numerical variation, comparison coverage, or another execution mismatch. At 20% research progress, a bounded diagnostic correction is more actionable than introducing recurrent-memory changes or elaborate activation patching.
idea.implementation_notes:
Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), returning metrics and metric_definitions. Retain existing embedding and sampled-margin probes. Use the actual view.model and preserve item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data and review_data contracts. Do not fabricate unavailable metadata or user traits.

Create a small deterministic fixture suite from this trial's public training histories: singleton, mixed-length, repeated-item and maximum-length histories, plus explicit empty rows. Fix candidate identities and order. Use actual supported model input widths. For left-padded nonempty rows, independently compute the maximum nonzero position; never use count-1. Empty rows require separate handling and must not be indexed with -1.

First cache one feature tensor F from one forward pass. Compare the actual _readout applied to F and its sequence mask with an independently gathered reference from that identical F, using the actual supplied signature. If the method is inaccessible, report skipped with a reason rather than substituting a surrogate. Test shapes, finiteness and comparison counts first. An exact same-tensor gather should agree exactly when the readout contract is a pure selection; if the implementation applies another operation, document and test that actual contract instead.

Next compare repeated forwards, singleton versus batch, row permutation with restored identities, and added-leading-padding configurations separately. Padding invariance is an expected property only when padding transitions are skipped by the trained implementation. Preserve atol=1e-5 and rtol=1e-4 for separate-forward comparisons and report elementwise violations of abs(actual-reference) <= atol + rtol*abs(reference). Do not relax thresholds merely to obtain a pass. Record feature, raw-score and ranking discrepancies separately. Do not claim pinned-evaluator rank parity without its ranking adapter.

Calibrate on temporary diagnostic wrappers, never checkpoint edits: count-1 readout on partially padded nonempty rows, swapped user rows with distinct histories, and permuted candidate identities with fixed supplied order. Include an unchanged wrapper control. A mutation is eligible only when it changes the relevant reference output; otherwise record equivalent-on-fixtures or inapplicable. Report a fault-by-check detection matrix, compared-element counts and unchanged-control false alarms. Synthetic tensors with distinct position values can establish readout-test sensitivity independently of learned weights; label these structural controls, not model behavior.

Exercise the actual exported predictor only through an available explicit adapter. Missing export access is skipped coverage, not agreement. Restore model modes, RNG states, hooks and temporary wrappers in finally blocks. Save scalar audit results beneath the trial directory and report diagnostic runtime. Resume only temporal measurements whose prerequisites have passed; unresolved export parity remains explicitly unresolved.

Keep the corrected GRU4Rec family, four category routes, one independently trained checkpoint per category, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs, 200 batches per epoch, single-GPU execution, and DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']. This audit needs no additional fitted model or score fusion. A proven model-semantic correction requires consistent retraining and matching changes to the predictor writer and loader; never modify only the probe and attribute altered semantics to the existing checkpoint. Preserve separate full-catalog recommendations for the twenty training simulator users. Use no other trials, hidden test files, external datasets or pretrained weights. Official host macro validation HR@10 remains the sole selection metric.
idea.pseudocode:
run_full_diagnosis(train_loader):
    save modes, RNG states and installed hooks
    try:
        set actual model to eval; enter inference_mode
        retain embedding and sampled-margin probes
        fixtures = deterministic_training_only_fixtures(seed=42)
        for fixture in fixtures:
            F = view.log2feats(fixture.sequence)
            validate feature shape and finiteness
            nonempty = any(sequence != 0, axis=1)
            j = maximum nonzero position for each nonempty row
            reference = independently gather F[row, j]
            actual = actual_readout(F, sequence) if supported
            record same-tensor comparison status, count and discrepancies
            check empty behavior separately
        test synthetic position-distinct tensors against actual readout
        for configuration in [repeat, singleton, batch, permuted_batch, added_padding]:
            execute fixed fixtures; restore row identities
            record semantic applicability and nonempty comparison coverage
            compare features and fixed-candidate scores elementwise
            record ranking changes only with an explicit ranking adapter
        for wrapper in [identity, wrong_index, row_swap, candidate_permutation]:
            install temporary wrapper without changing parameters
            establish whether mutation changes reference outputs
            run applicable checks; record detection or equivalent/inapplicable status
            remove wrapper
        if explicit exported-predictor adapter exists:
            compare actual predictor outputs on all four category routes
        else:
            record export parity as skipped with reason
        if temporal prerequisites pass:
            run prespecified full-shuffle and final-item-fixed panel
        else:
            return affected temporal metrics as null with reasons
        record runtime and fault-by-check coverage
    finally:
        restore wrappers, hooks, modes and RNG states
    return {metrics, metric_definitions}

diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis):
    include measured metrics, definitions, coverage and mutation results
    distinguish same-tensor indexing failures from separate-forward discrepancies
    distinguish missing comparisons from executed agreement
    prohibit inferred intent, causal user preferences or unmeasured validation gains

originality.positive: Combines same-tensor readout identity and fault-detection calibration around a specific unresolved GRU4Rec diagnostic inconsistency.
originality.negative: Independent indexing references, metamorphic checks and mutation testing are established techniques; the contribution is their focused integration.

future_potential.positive: Can resolve the immediate blocker and establish trustworthy prerequisites for subsequent recurrent-memory and temporal-sensitivity experiments.
future_potential.negative: Passing bounded fixtures provides limited execution coverage and does not demonstrate recommendation improvement or generalization.

code_difficulty.positive: Requires only bounded inference, small fixtures and temporary wrappers, without fitting another predictor or changing the architecture.
code_difficulty.negative: Correct handling of actual readout signatures, equivalent mutations, state restoration and exported-predictor coverage requires care.

related_work.title: PyTorch GRU documentation
contributions: Documents per-position recurrent outputs and final hidden states, supporting explicit readout-contract checks.
limitations: Does not establish the supplied model's padding semantics or demonstrate that its reported discrepancy is an indexing defect.

related_work.title: PyTorch Numerical accuracy
contributions: Explains why mathematically equivalent batched and singleton computations need not be bitwise identical.
limitations: Numerical caveats cannot justify semantic mismatches or retrospective tolerance relaxation.

related_work.title: Beyond Accuracy: Behavioral Testing of NLP Models with CheckList
contributions: Organizes behavioral testing around minimum functionality, invariance and directional expectations.
limitations: Its application to GRU4Rec execution auditing is a proposed adaptation rather than a validated recommendation benchmark.

related_work.title: DeepMutation
contributions: Uses injected model faults to assess test effectiveness, motivating a diagnostic fault-detection matrix.
limitations: Reported experiments concern image classifiers; temporary GRU4Rec wrapper mutations require independent calibration.

related_work.title: Towards Best Practices of Activation Patching in Language Models: Metrics and Methods
contributions: Shows that corruption methods and evaluation metrics materially affect activation-patching conclusions.
limitations: Recurrent recommendation patching is an extrapolation and requires faithful state replay and controlled candidates.

related_work.title: Theory of Gating in Recurrent Neural Networks
contributions: Connects recurrent gates with memory timescales and context-dependent state dynamics.
limitations: Gate dynamics alone do not establish task-relevant forgetting or improved recommendation ranking.

related_work.title: FEVER: a Large-scale Dataset for Fact Extraction and VERification
contributions: Provides an evidence-linked supported, refuted and insufficient-information annotation pattern.
limitations: Textual evidence about item specifications cannot establish a user's current requirements, ownership or willingness to choose.
